scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Pulimaranja Thondachan originates in the North Malabar region of Kerala, specifically associated with the Pulayar community in the Kannur and Kasargod districts.
The tradition stems from the legend of Madai Kari Kurikkal, a farm worker's son who trained in eighteen kalaris and acquired magical shapeshifting abilities.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Worshipped as a theyyam deity by the Pulayar community, commemorating Madai Kari Kurikkal, whose tragic transformation and disappearance into the forest led to his veneration following the Alladam lord's recurring insanity.
Today it is a living tradition.
